articles.title: Upper Tribunal overturns landlord’s HMO penalty in ‘rack rent’ ruling
articles.summary:
Judge rules landlord receiving less than two-thirds of HMO income was not legally in control of the property.
The post Upper Tribunal overturns landlord’s HMO penalty in ‘rack rent’ ruling appeared first on The Negotiator.
articles.ai_summary:
- The Upper Tribunal ruled that a landlord, earning under two-thirds of the income from a House in Multiple Occupation (HMO), does not legally control the property, overturning a previous penalty.
- This landmark decision clarifies the legal standing of landlords in "rack rent" situations, impacting compliance requirements for HMO management.
